chose: an edit's spec problems are said per session and file until they change: the written file alone is parsed, its problems' messages (lines aside) are its signature, the file is named with every problem when the signature differs from what this session was told, and forgotten when clean
over: only problems new since before the edit (the pre-edit text is not in the event; rebuilding it from old_string/new_string fails for Write, MultiEdit, patches and shell writes); a full loadSpecModel at the edit (whole-model problems, over the tool hook budget on a real project); saying every problem at every edit of the file (a standing problem in a busy spec would train the reader to skip the line)
because: it mirrors how a literal mirror is said once per session and forgotten when it agrees, reports only files the edit wrote so a problem elsewhere never repeats, and one file's parse costs milliseconds; problems only the model sees stay with spec --check and the stop

steps.text: classify it: record the defect with --class, --introduced and --caught, or classify one already recorded (classify <defect-id>); a class declared nowhere is declared once first, as the property class <name> of defect (lexicon propose define defect)
steps.leaves: the defect's or the classification's id

steps.text: name what let the bug be written (the state a value can hold that it never should, or a second way to do what one function should do alone), then sweep the codebase for every sibling of that shape and record the sweep: what was searched and each sibling found, or that it found none
steps.leaves: the representable shape, and the sweep

steps.text: fix it so the code cannot express it again, in preference to a check at the site: one door every caller must pass (a function or class its module keeps private, so the compiler, or a totality oracle where the language has no such check, refuses any other caller), a type that cannot hold the bad value, a walk with a stack of its own rather than recursion over what input controls, a fact derived where it is needed rather than kept twice; route every sibling the sweep found through it. When the dead-end reading names the defect's component (DEAD END in spec --check, Dead ends in orient), weigh a different design for that component before adding any such door to the one it has, and record the choice, redesign or keep, as a decision
steps.leaves: the door, type or derivation, and the siblings now routed through it; at a dead end, the decision choosing the design

steps.text: guard or decide: name an invariant that fails on any second way to write the bug, a chokepoint the compiler grades or a totality oracle that reads the code and refuses each other door (another call, a name held under an alias, a module asked for by string), adding the bullet when none exists; or record a decision saying why fixing the instance suffices, or that only time or a scheduler can show the bug (a cost, a race), bounding it structurally all the same (a size every read passes, a lock only one process can take)
steps.leaves: the guard's <component folder>/<invariant> or the decision's id

steps.text: refute the guard: witness a refutation of it, staging a second way to write the bug rather than replaying the instance
record the close: resolved <defect-id> --because "<what fixed it, and the sweep>" with --guard <component folder>/<invariant> or --decision <id>, then run spec --check
steps.leaves: the resolution's id; spec --check names no close with neither

pitfalls: the symbolic-link spelling was fixed where the upgrade test found it, and only a sweep of the same comparison found the second site, in practice delivery's cd routing (df-ccfd4309, 4b1890f)
a second door opened past the warm server's chokepoint reached main because nothing that ran before the merge checked chokepoints; a guard protects only where it runs (df-5961bdb2)
an ownership defect was fixed for one kernel practice when its class was every kernel practice of every release; the guard that held was the one that read them all (df-36efa8f2, 4b1890f)

the parse store's defences were checks written at each of its file system calls, and three blind reviews in a row found one more call without its check; one gateway, unexported and held by a parse of its module, was the fix that held (ca263d3, df-8b32c22b)

the gateway's totality oracle read only node:fs imported by name, so a require made with createRequire and the file system asked of process.getBuiltinModule each wrote past it with the test green (df-69c8ab4d)
a recursion over a parse tree was kept when its function was rewritten, so a file nested deep enough crashed every reading (df-6e6c2b80)

src/plugins, home of the parse store, collected 26 defects in 7 classes over 11 commits of blind review, each round closed by a check at the site its reviewer found and a test that the check existed, and the next round found faults in those checks (df-7c50adfe, df-aad5bf07, df-8b32c22b, df-2456bd98, df-69c8ab4d, df-ff68d46c, df-586f6367); the representation was the defect, a security-relevant cache inside the untrusted repository kept as mutable shared state, and nothing said so until the dead-end reading

3.evidence: the parser refuses the shape, and the edit hook parses the written spec

5.evidence: refutation witnessed: a second way staged for the parser guard, the alarm left out of the context for the hook guard

6.evidence: resolved; spec --check names no close with neither
